#### INDIAN NATIONAL CONGRESS

#### ASSOCIATIONS FORMED BEFORE CONGRESS

  • Few regional level associations were formed before Congress.
  1. 1. Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha
  • 1836: It was started by associates of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
  1. 2. East India Association
  • 1866: It was founded by Dadabhai Naoroji in London.
  1. 3. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
  • 1870: It was started by M G Ranade (in Maharashtra).
  1. 4. Indian League
  • 1875: It was founded by Sisir Kumar Ghosh.
  • He founded Bengali newspaper: Amrita Bazar Patrika.
  1. 5. Indian National Association
  • 1876: It was founded by Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose.
  1. 6. Madras Mahajan Sabha
  • 1884: It was founded by M. Viraraghavachari, G. Subramanian Iyer and P. Ananda Charlu.
  1. 7. Bombay Presidency Association
  • 1885: It was founded by Pherozeshah Mehta, K. T. Telang, and Badruddin Tyabji.

DADABHAI NAOROJI

  • He was the first Indian British member of Parliament.
  • He presided three sessions of Congress (1886, 1893, 1906).
  • He prepared the first estimate of the National Income of India in 1876 (he is also known as "Father of National Income in India").
  • He used the term "Swaraj" for the first time.
  • He is also known as "Grand Old Man of India".
  • Rast Goftar (a weekly newspaper by him for Parsi community) and Voice of India.
  • Book written: "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (explains the Drain of Wealth Theory).
  • He also started a movement called "Rahnumae Mazdayasnan Sabha" in 1851 along with Naoroji Furdonji and S.S. Bengalee.

#### DIFFERENT THEORIES

  • Safety Valve Theory: Lala Lajpat Rai (monthly magazine by him: Young India).
  • Conspiracy Theory: R. P. Dutt.
  • Lightning Conductor Theory: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
Dufferin was the Viceroy at the time of formation of Congress and called Congress a "Factory of Sedition".

#### IMPORTANT SESSIONS OF CONGRESS

  • First Session: 1885 → Headed by W. C. Banerjee in Bombay, where 72 Delegates attended it.
  • Second Session: 1886 → Headed by Dadabhai Naoroji in Calcutta, where 434 Delegates attended it.
  • Third Session: 1887 → Headed by Badruddin Tyabji in Calcutta. He was the first Muslim President of Congress.
  • Fourth Session: 1888 → Headed by George Yule in Allahabad. He was the first British President of Congress.
  • 1896: Held in Calcutta. Our National Song, Vande Mataram was sung for the first time by Rabindranath Tagore (written by: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee).
  • 1901: Held in Calcutta. Mahatma Gandhi participated in this INC Session for the first time.
  • 1905: Headed by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in Benaras. Swadeshi Movement was formally adopted here.
  • 1906: Headed by Dadabhai Naoroji in Calcutta. Four resolutions: Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education were adopted.
  • 1907: Headed by Rash Behari Ghosh in Surat. In this Session the Congress split into Extremists and Moderates.
  • 1911: Held in Calcutta. Our National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana written by Rabindranath Tagore was first sung in this Session.
  • 1916: Headed by Ambika Charan Mazumdar in Lucknow leading to merger of Congress. A Joint Pact also known as Lucknow Pact was signed between the Muslim League and Indian National Congress.
  • 1917: Headed by Annie Besant in Calcutta (first Women President of Congress).
  • 1924: Headed by Mahatma Gandhi (only Session presided by him) in Belgaum (Karnataka).
  • 1925: Headed by Sarojini Naidu (first Indian women President of Congress and first women Governor of India state (Uttar Pradesh)) in Kanpur.
  • 1929: Headed by Jawaharlal Nehru in Lahore. The INC passed the resolution for complete independence or Purna Swaraj (January 26, 1930 was officially declared to be celebrated as first Independence Day).
  • 1931: Headed by Sardar Patel in Karachi.
  • 1937: Headed by J L Nehru in Faizpur (first Session to be held in a village).

1938-1939: Mahatma Gandhi Vs Subhash Chandra Bose

  • In 1938 Session, held at Haripura (Gujarat) and S C Bose was elected as President of INC.

#### INDIAN NATIONAL CONGRESS

  • In 1939 Session, held at Tripuri and S C Bose was re-elected by defeating Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but later S C Bose resigned.
  • Rajendra Prasad was elected as President in 1939.
  • Madan Mohan Malviya presided INC Session most number of times.
  • JB Kriplani: President during the time of Independence.
  • Youngest President of INC: Abul Kalam Azad.
\\Note: It is advisable to read about the Sessions after you have read the entire Modern History.

VICEROYS (post-1858)

The post-1858 Crown-reign viceroys. Per T12 Bucket 3.3, this section was
split out from history/25 - Governor-General and Viceroy.md and appended
here as the freedom-fight-era administrative anchor (INC L2). New T01 L3:
history.indian_national_congress.viceroys.

Lord Canning (1856-1857)

  • He became the 1st Viceroy of India.
  • 1857 Revolt.
  • Government of India Act (1858) was passed.

Lord Mayo (1860-1872)

  • 1st Unsynchronised (not complete) Census was held during his tenure (1872).
  • He established Statistical Survey of India.
  • Sher Ali Afridi killed him in Andaman Jail.

Lord Lytton (1876-1880)

  • Arms Act (1878).
  • He brought Vernacular Press Act (1878) to ban local newspapers.
  • First Delhi Durbar (1877) to proclaim Queen Victoria as Empress of India.
  • 2nd Afghan War (1878-1880).
  • He lowered the maximum age of eligibility for Civil Services (reduced the age from 21 to 19 years).
"Bengal Gazette" by James Augustus Hickey was the 1st Newspaper in India (1780).

Lord Ripon (1880-1884)

  • Ilbert bill was introduced in 1883.
  • He repealed Vernacular Press Act.
  • 1st Synchronised (complete) Census held during his tenure (1881).
  • He is known as Father of Local Self-Government.
  • Hunter Commission (1882) was setup which was related to Education.
  • 1st Factory Act (1881).

Lord Dufferin (1884-1888)

  • Formation of INC (1885).

Lord Curzon (1899-1905)

  • Partition of Bengal (1905).
  • Indian Universities Act.
  • Calcutta Corporation Act.
  • Curzon-Kitchener controversy.
  • Young Husband Mission (to Tibet).

Lord Minto II (1905-1910)

  • Muslim League formation (1906) by Aga Khan.
  • Surat Split.

Lord Hardinge II (1910-1916)

  • 3rd Delhi Durbar for King George (1911).
  • During his tenure, capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
  • Royal Commission on Civil Services was appointed in 1912.

Lord Chelmsford (1916-1921)

  • Government of India Act, also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919).
  • Rowlatt Act (1919).
  • Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919).

Lord Reading (1921-1926)

  • Chauri Chaura Incident (1922).
  • Kakori Train Incident (1925).
  • Establishment of Swaraj Party (1923).
  • Repeal of Press Act (1910) and Rowlatt Act (1919).

Lord Irwin (1926-1931)

  • Visit of Simon Commission (1928).
  • Lahore Session of Congress (1929).
  • Dandi March (1930).
  • 1st Round Table Conference.

Lord Willingdon (1931-1936)

  • 2nd Round Table Conference.
  • 3rd Round Table Conference.
  • Government of India Act (1935).

Lord Linlithgow (1936-1941)

  • World War II.
  • August Offer (1940).
  • Individual Satyagrah (1940).
  • Quit India Movement (1942).
  • Cripps Mission (1942).

Lord Wavell (1944-1947)

  • CR Formula (1944).
  • Wavell Plan (1945).
  • Cabinet Mission Proposals (1946).
  • Observance of Direct Action Day (16 August 1946).
  • Lord Mountbatten (1947-48) → Last British Governor General of India.
  • Only Indian Governor General of India: C. Rajagopalachari.
